bib.title: DeepSearch: Overcome the Bottleneck of Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards via Monte Carlo Tree Search

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "DeepSearch: Overcome the Bottleneck of Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards via Tree-Based Search". First author Fang Wu (Stanford). Co-first authors Weihao Xuan and Heli Qi. Corresponding author Yejin Choi. Venue: ICLR 2026 conference paper. arXiv 2509.25454v4, dated 6 Apr 2026 on the PDF. The v1 month is not printed; arXiv ID 2509 suggests Sept 2025. Local file: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/generative-ai/05-RL/sources/wu-2025-deepsearch.pdf

COVERAGE: 26 of 26 pages (86,608 chars). Main text, refs (skimmed), Appendices A–E and Limitations were all read. Pages 20–26 are qualitative traces. I read only the starts of the later traces and the closing text. Several tables are flattened by extraction.

Confirmed: this is MCTS inside RLVR training. It bears most on note 08 (RLVR plateaus, exploration), then 01 (credit assignment) and 09/10 (engineering and cost).

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. MCTS in the training loop (not only at inference) beats the prior 1.5B state of the art by 1.25 points. Setup: init Nemotron-Research-Reasoning-Qwen-1.5B v2, trained on DeepMath-103K. Pass@1 estimated from n=32 samples, six math benchmarks.
 number: 62.95 vs 61.70 average. AIME24 53.65 vs 51.77, AMC23 90.39 vs 88.83.
 quote: "DeepSearch-1.5B achieves 62.95% average accuracy, outperforming all baselines, including the previous best Nemotron-Research-Reasoning-Qwen-1.5B v2 (61.70%)."
 where: p7 and Table 1, p8
2. Extended plain RLVR plateaus; DeepSearch uses far fewer GPU hours. Setup: Table 2, DAPO extended training versus Tree-GRPO. Training is 16xH100 96GB; evaluation is 128xH100. Table 2 says "trained from DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B", but A.1 says the init is Nemotron v2 (an inconsistency in the paper).
 number: DAPO+KL +1,875 steps = 1,883.2 GPU h, 62.02. +325 steps = 326.4 h, 61.78. +785 steps = 788.8 h, 62.08. DeepSearch +50 steps = ~330 GPU h, 62.95. Claimed 5.7x fewer GPU hours than 1,883.2 h. Also claimed 72x efficiency versus Nemotron v2's 24,000 GPU h.
 quote: "With only 50 additional training steps, DeepSearch reaches 62.95% accuracy using 330 GPU hours—outperforming the most extensive baseline (1,883.2 hours) while using 5.7×fewer resources."
 where: p8, Table 2
3. Component ablation (Table 4, avg over six benchmarks, base 61.70). Vanilla DeepSearch 60.27 is below base. New q-update with coarse scores 61.38. Fine-grained scores 61.85. Standard advantage normalization 62.27. Mean-only normalization 62.32. Adding global frontier selection 62.95 ("the largest single improvement"). Note that most of the gain over base comes from the q-update, node-level advantages and normalization, not the search alone. Single run, no variance reported.
 quote: "+ Frontier Selection 53.65 35.42 90.39 92.53 40.00 65.72 62.95"
 where: p10, Table 4
4. Negative-sample choice: when MCTS finds no correct answer, backprop the lowest-entropy (most confident) wrong trajectory. Avg: most confident 62.95, random 62.09, least confident 61.90.
 quote: "achieves the best average performance (+0.86 over random and +1.05 over least confident)"
 where: p10, Table 5
5. Global frontier selection versus vanilla UCT, on 1.2K very hard DeepMath problems. Iterations fell from 209.6 to 187.7 (10.4%). Trajectory reward went from -0.82 to -0.65. A linear depth bonus cut per-tree time by 59% (1179.6 s to 480.9 s) but lowered reward to -0.76. The default is sqrt(d/dT), λ1=0.4, λ3=0.01.
 where: p9, Table 3
6. Replay buffer progressively caches solutions (Table 6, 5 rounds). The cached share grows from 0% (round 1, 13,658 unsolved) to 33.2% (round 5: 2,894 cached, 5,829 unsolved). Filtering uses Pass1@K, K=4, δ=25%.
 where: p17
7. Cost profile: generation is the bottleneck. tgenerate = 1060.76 ms per tree, >99% of per-tree time. CPU-side MCTS logic is a few ms. Prefill re-encoding of prefixes dominates, and 256-token expansion steps were best among 128/256/512/1024.
 where: p16, p18

Method in brief: node = 256-token step, 8 children, max depth 64, UCT λ=2.0 for sibling choice. Global frontier score F = λ1·tanh(Qparent) + λ2·H + λ3·sqrt(d/dT). Asymmetric constrained q-backup with depth decay γmin=0.1. Tree-GRPO has tanh soft clipping of q, DAPO Clip-Higher (0.2/0.28), no KL, and mean-only advantage Â = q(sj) − µ. Terminal reward is +1 for correct and −1 for incorrect or incomplete. It degrades to DAPO if the outcome reward is used for all nodes.

Hyperparameters: lr 1e-6, global batch 256, mini-batch 32, 8 rollouts per prompt, 16,384 response tokens, framework veRL, 100 training steps with checkpoint every 5 (A.5), 5 adaptive rounds.

LIMITS
- Math only, one 1.5B model, one training dataset. No other scales or domains were tested.
- Seeds and variance are not reported for the benchmark tables, only mean±sd for search statistics (Table 3). Gains are ~1 point.
- The "5.7x" and "72x" figures compare against the authors' own DAPO extension. Table 2's GPU-hour cell is garbled in the extraction ("33062.95").
- The paper concedes that it needs verifiable rewards, and that the frontier function and expansion width are fixed heuristics, not learned (suggests an AlphaZero-style controller).
- Intro frames "plateau after thousands of steps" via ProRL (Liu 2025a) and does not re-test it directly. The Figure 2 trend is linear over 20 h only.
- Qualitative claim that outputs have fewer "wait" loops rests on 6 cherry-picked cases (App. E).

BUILDS ON: ProRL (Liu et al., 2025a) and Nemotron 1.5B v2 as base; DAPO (Yu et al., 2025) for Clip-Higher and dynamic batching; GRPO (Shao et al., 2024); UCT (Kocsis & Szepesvári, 2006); AlphaGo (Silver et al., 2016); DeepScaleR (Luo et al., 2025b); DeepMath-103K (He et al., 2025c); veRL/HybridFlow (Sheng et al., 2024); Hochlehnert et al. (2025) for the eval protocol; Bereket & Leskovec (2025) for mean-only normalization; Chu et al. (2025) for sequence-level normalization.

CODE: Algorithm 1 pseudocode, p19. Key rule, Eq. 7: "F(s)=λ1×tanh(Qparent(s)) + λ2×H(πθ(s|os)) + λ3×D(d(s))" (p5).

FIGURES: Fig. 1 (p2) shows the framework: frontier selection, entropy-guided negative, replay buffer, Tree-GRPO. Fig. 2 (p8) plots DAPO versus DeepSearch average (AIME24/25, AMC23) over 20 h after 3K RLVR steps, with a steeper DeepSearch slope. I did not render figures.

QUOTES FOR NOTES
- p1: "contemporary studies have documented training plateaus after thousands of optimization steps, i.e., notable decreases in performance gains despite increased computational investment."
- p8: "extended training exhibits diminishing returns: 325 additional steps achieve 61.78% accuracy using 326.4 GPU hours, whereas 1,875 steps plateau at 62.02% accuracy despite consuming 1,883.2 GPU hours."
- p8: "The superior convergence properties suggest that RLVR bottlenecks stem from the quality of exploration rather than from insufficient training time."

PROBLEMS: None embedded. Extraction garbles Table 2's last row, and the table header says the init is R1-Distill while A.1 says Nemotron v2. The comparison is on one model and ~1 point; treat the "new direction" framing as the authors' own.
